$comment: The event-type vocabulary that clients are allowed to put on the wire.
This file exists because the vocabulary was hand-authored twice with no
mechanical link between the copies: AscendaTelemetryEventType in
ai-engineer-tools' packages/tool-contract (TypeScript), and
WorkloadCategoryMap in Services/ToolTelemetryCatalog.cs (C#). Drift between
them did not fail a build; it surfaced as rows in the 'unclassified' bucket
months later, which is how @ascenda-one/history-import lost seven months of
one person's history behind a 2xx.
Ownership: this file is the source of truth for the wire vocabulary. The C#
side pins it in ToolPairingCatalogValidationTests; the TypeScript side should
vendor a copy and assert equality against its union in its own test, so a name
added on one side and not the other fails a build rather than a dashboard.
Adding a type: add it here, add it to WorkloadCategoryMap with a category (a
type present here but absent there would classify as 'unclassified' and is
caught by the contract test), and add it to the TypeScript union.
The C# catalog is deliberately a superset of this list. It also classifies
supervision_interruption and the coarse workflow/HRIS types (email_activity,
message_activity, calendar_block), which the org activity-signals door
produces internally via CoarseSignalTypeMap rather than accepting from a
paired client. Those are not client-emittable and so are not on this list.
